Forecast Discussion

High pressure building into the Northeast wedges down the east side of the Appalachians today through the weekend. Meteorologists call this a "dry wedge" as there is no precipitation associated with it, just cool, dry air.

The northeasterly winds provide limited moisture for some clouds here and there. Temperatures cool down a little today and a little more tomorrow. Our streak of pleasant fall weather continues.

The center of the high shifts eastward Monday allowing for an increase in afternoon temperatures Monday and Tuesday but overnight temperatures will remain chilly.

A weakening cold front moves into the area Wednesday but it is dry and the slightly cooler air only lasts a day or so.

It appears our next chance of rain will be in early November.
